headline: Foundation Stone Laid for ‘Healing Fins’ – Maharashtra’s First Multispecialty Fish Clinic & Mobile Fish Care Unit at ICAR-CIFE, Mumbai | ICAR
content: The Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony of “Healing Fins” – Maharashtra’s First Multispecialty Fish Clinic & Mobile Fish Care Unit was held today, at the ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Education, Mumbai. The foundation stone was laid by the Chief Guest, Advocate Ashish Shelar, Minister of Information Technology & Cultural Affairs and Guardian Minister, Mumbai Suburban, Government of Maharashtra. The ceremony was graced by Haroon Rashid Khan, Member of Legislative Assembly, Versova Constituency; Saurabh Katiyar, District Collector, Mumbai Suburban; Sanjay Kumar Shinde; and N. P. Sahu, Director, ICAR-CIFE, Mumbai, along with other dignitaries. The “Healing Fins” facility is being established within the ICAR-CIFE campus by the Aquatic Environment and Health Management (AEHM) Division, with financial support from the District Planning Committee, Mumbai Suburban, Government of Maharashtra. Located at Versova, the facility aims to provide comprehensive fish health services, including disease diagnosis and treatment, catering to fish farmers, shrimp farmers, aquarium owners, and ornamental fish hobbyists. The initiative adopts a four-tier approach encompassing clinical services, mobile outreach, advanced diagnostics, and telehealth services to ensure holistic fish health management. A Mobile Fish Care Unit has also been integrated to deliver on-site services, enabling timely treatment and technical advisory support at farm and field levels. The programme commenced with a welcome address by Dr. N. P. Sahu, who highlighted the significance of the initiative. This was followed by a detailed presentation by Megha K. Bedekar, Principal Scientist, Head of AEHM Division, and Principal Investigator of the project, who elaborated on the concept, infrastructure, and operational framework of the clinic and mobile unit. During the programme, Shri Haroon Rashid Khan underscored the importance of establishing such a facility in a metropolitan region and its potential benefits to stakeholders in the fisheries sector. The dignitaries also visited key facilities of ICAR-CIFE, including the Aquatic Biodiversity Museum and Aquarium, and appreciated the institute’s contributions to fisheries education, research, and extension. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks by Aishwarya Ranadive, Assistant Commissioner of Fisheries, Mumbai Suburban. The event witnessed the participation of more than 250 attendees, including Heads of Divisions, scientists, students, representatives of fishermen societies, and staff of the Mumbai Suburban Committee.

headline: Row over power purchase snowballing in Keralam
content: Thiruvananthapuram: The opposition CPI(M) in Keralam has raised suspicion of corruption in the Congress government's decision to purchase power from GNA Energy, a Haryana based OTC platform, overlooking an offer from Himachal Pradesh. Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan even alleged that an artificial power crisis was being created to purchase power at higher price even as power at lower rates would be available in view of the rains received in many states. .Soaring heat, inadequate rains plunge Kerala into acute crisis: State imposes up to one hour power cuts.Vijayan also said that the decision to purchase power from an OTC platform instead of a producer also deepens the mystery as private power producers could be getting the benefit of the deal. The differences within the Congress government over the economic viability of the power purchase is also helping the opposition to step up the attack against the V D Satheesan government. Meanwhile, Satheesan denied Vijayan's allegations and maintained that while considering the average price of the power during the peak hours and non peak hours the offer by GNA was more viable. He also said that even the previous left front government had purchased power from the same firm. He also denied the allegations that the power crisis was an artificial one by citing reports. The fresh row was triggered after a report of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) citing the purchasing power from GNA would lead to an additional financial burden of Rs. 726 crore compared to that from Himachal. KSEB also cited that Himachal's proposal would also help in addressing the peak hour shortage GNA has offered round the clock supply of 500 MW at Rs. 8.48 per unit. KSEB cited that it could lead to surplus power during day time. Himachal had offered power at Rs. 14.50 per unit, which KSEB was hopeful of reducing to Rs. 12.50 per unit through negotiations. The Chief Minister's justification was that considering the average costs, the one by GNA would be more profitable for the state even if there is surplus during the day time.

headline: Supreme Court settles decade-old energy dispute, Himachal to get 11,973 MU electricity from Punjab, Haryana
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Monday brought the curtain down on a decades-long energy dispute between Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Haryana over the payment of dues arising from Bhakra Beas Management Board projects since 1966. .A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana accepted the Centre’s cashless proposal on payment of dues in energy terms to Himachal Pradesh by Punjab and Haryana. .The top court said the arrangement will be as per a 2011 apex court verdict settling power dues arising out of Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydro projects since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh at the rate of 7.19 per cent. .Cannot convict one accused alone under common intention charge when co-accused are acquitted: Supreme Court.It said Punjab and Haryana will pay Himachal Pradesh 11,973 million units of electricity over a period of 20 years. .Punjab government initially opposed the Centre’s proposal for payment of energy arrears in 15 years but later sought implementation of the plan over a period of 30 years, while Himachal Pradesh sought implementation within 10 years. .Under the proposal, an adjustment of Rs 420 crore towards historical capital costs incurred in constructing the dams has been factored into the settlement, and Himachal Pradesh will not have to pay anything to Punjab and Haryana. .The original entitlement was calculated at 13,066 million units by the Central Electricity Authority. .According to the 2011 decision of the apex court, the share of Himachal was fixed at 7.19 per cent, while that of Punjab and Haryana was fixed at 51.80 per cent and 37.51 per cent, respectively. .Rajasthan's share largely remained unaffected, while the share of Chandigarh was fixed at 3.50 per cent. .According to the 2011 decision, Himachal was to get a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977, and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.

headline: Aarti Drugs' Baddi facility in Himachal Pradesh gets 3 US FDA Form 483 observations
content: Aarti Drugs Ltd on Friday said its subsidiary, Pinnacle Life Science Private Ltd, received three inspectional observations in Form 483 from the United States Food and Drug Administration following an inspection of its formulations manufacturing facility in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh.The US FDA inspected the facility from November 2 to November 6, 2026. Aarti Drugs said none of the three observations was related to data integrity and that the company would work closely with the US regulator to resolve all the points.In a regulatory filing, Aarti Drugs said the observations would have no impact on the financial, operational or other activities of the company. It also stated that there was no financial or operational impact on Pinnacle Life Science. The company received the Form 483 communication on November 6, the date on which the inspection concluded.ALSO READ | Aarti Drugs Q2 Results: Net profit soars 83% on stronger margins, revenue growthAarti Drugs said it would work closely with the US FDA to address the three inspectional observations received at the conclusion of the inspection. The company did not specify the individual observations in its filing. It reiterated that none of the points was related to data integrity.What is a Form 483A Form 483 is a list of observations made during the inspection and is issued by the USFDA inspectors post the completion of the inspection. The inspector will communicate and explain these observations to the supplier during the closing conference. But a Form 483 does not represent a final FDA determination regarding the facility’s GMP compliance.Post Form 483 is issued, the company is given 15 days time to submit its response to the USFDA explaining what steps will the company take to resolve the observations made by USFDA.ALSO READ | Aarti Drugs sees healthy FY27 growth as prices remain firm, capacity expandsShares of Aarti Drugs Ltd ended at ₹445.90, up by ₹1.60, or 0.36%, on the BSE.

headline: Immunologist Manali Mukherjee receives Falling Walls Women's Impact Award for her work on Long Covid
content: The prestigious international award recognizes Mukherjee’s patient-centred, evidence-based research on Long COVID. McMaster respiratory immunologist Manali Mukherjee has been honoured at the 2026 Falling Walls Science Summit in Berlin for research that reveals the biological basis of Long COVID. Mukherjee, an associate professor of medicine, is a 2026 Falling Walls Winner in the Women’s Impact Award category and a Science Breakthrough of the Year winner for her work, “Breaking the Wall of Long COVID Denial: With Immunology, Not Opinion.” The societal and institutional fatigue linked to the pandemic has curtailed research around the long-term impacts of COVID-19 on patients, some of whom developed autoimmune diseases after being perfectly healthy prior to their illness, said Mukherjee, who is also the AstraZeneca Chair in Respiratory Diseases. “The only fatigue that should be associated with Long COVID is the fatigue of the people who are suffering from it,” said Mukherjee. “That’s the fatigue we should be addressing. There should not be fatigue in policymakers or those responsible for funding and conducting research.”

headline: CM’s constituency visits political drama, won’t save Cong govt: BJP
content: Shimla: The Himachal Pradesh BJP on Friday accused chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu of resorting to “political drama” through constituency visits and multi-crore announcements ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, alleging that the Congress govt had lost public confidence.Addressing a news conference, BJP state media in charge and Naina Devi MLA Randhir Sharma questioned the financial credibility of the announcements, claiming govt lacked funds for basic road repairs, HRTC bus maintenance and MLA development works. He also demanded details of budgetary provisions for the new promises.Accusing the state govt of corruption and diversion of disaster relief funds, Sharma demanded a white paper detailing central assistance received under the SDRF (State Disaster Response Fund), the NDRF (National Disaster Response Fund) and the PDNA (Post Disaster Needs Assessment), along with department-wise allocations, constituency-wise expenditure, contractors and payments.He claimed Rs 2,006 crore had been approved under the PDNA, including a central share of Rs 1,504 crore, of which Rs 1,053 crore was released in July and Dec 2025.Sharma also alleged irregularities in public works department tendering and political discrimination in reconstruction works, demanding an independent probe into payments allegedly made without execution of work.On the Supreme Court’s verdict on the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), Sharma said it was the result of successive govts’ efforts since 1996 and not any single regime’s achievement.He also opposed the proposed public-private partnership (PPP) transfer of Hotel Peterhof in Shimla.The BJP functionary further questioned unfulfilled Congress guarantees, including Rs 1,500 monthly assistance for women and 300 units of free electricity.
